messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int f(int n) { if (n <= 0) return 0; return 1 + f(n); }

Question: What is f(2)?
The student answered: 2

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The recursive call moves toward the base case on its own

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: Hinglish: romanised Hindi mixed with English programming words, 6 to 16 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["n=2 hai toh f(2) call hoga aur andar jaake apne aap base case tak pahunch jayega, isliye 1+1=2.", "Har baar recursion andar jaata hai, toh 1+1 add karke 2 aa jayega, bas.", "f(n) khud ko call karta hai aur n chhota ho jaata hai, toh 2 baar count hoga, answer 2.", "Jab tak n<=0 nahi hota, function andar chalta rehta hai, 2 ke liye 2 return karega.", "Recursive call khud base case ki taraf badhta hai, isliye f(2) mein 1+1=2 sahi hai."]}

sentences: n=2 hai toh f(2) call hoga aur andar jaake apne aap base case tak pahunch jayega, isliye 1+1=2.
Har baar recursion andar jaata hai, toh 1+1 add karke 2 aa jayega, bas.
f(n) khud ko call karta hai aur n chhota ho jaata hai, toh 2 baar count hoga, answer 2.
Jab tak n<=0 nahi hota, function andar chalta rehta hai, 2 ke liye 2 return karega.
Recursive call khud base case ki taraf badhta hai, isliye f(2) mein 1+1=2 sahi hai.
